outline.description: This chapter introduces the parties, the employment relationship, the policy change that triggered the lawsuit, the statutory claims Cohen asserted, Consilio's payment of overtime wages and liquidated damages, and the procedural posture leading to summary judgment.
subtopics: The parties and employment relationship: Consilio as a legal document review company and Cohen as an hourly licensed attorney document reviewer
The July 2019 email announcing the new overtime policy eliminating premium pay
Cohen's August 2020 lawsuit asserting claims under the MPWA, MFLSA, and MWTA
Consilio's payment of $256,010.01 in overtime wages and liquidated damages to Minnesota document reviewers
The parties' stipulations regarding payment of overtime wages and liquidated damages
The disputed penalty amounts under each statute
The parties' agreement to proceed by summary judgment before further discovery
The district court's grant of summary judgment to Consilio on all claims

outline.chapter_title: The MPWA Claim: Statutory Interpretation of Penalty Provisions
outline.description: This chapter examines the court's analysis of whether a private employee may seek average daily wage penalties under the Minnesota Payment of Wages Act, focusing on principles of statutory interpretation and legislative intent.
subtopics: The statutory framework: Minn. Stat. §§ 181.171 and 181.101
Cohen's argument that the plain language of § 181.101 authorizes employees to seek penalties
The court's textual analysis showing penalties are available only through the Commissioner
The role of the Commissioner under § 181.101(a): serving demands and collecting penalties
The statute's reservation to employees of the right to 'prosecut[e] a claim for wages'
Comparative statutory analysis: §§ 181.13 and 181.14, which explicitly authorize employees to collect penalties
The 'legislature knows how' canon of statutory construction
Affirmance of the district court's grant of summary judgment on the MPWA claim

outline.chapter_title: The MFLSA Claim: Standing and Mootness in Civil Penalty Actions
outline.description: This chapter explores the jurisdictional issues raised by the court regarding Cohen's claim for statutory penalties under the MFLSA, including standing requirements, the relationship between standing and mootness, and the voluntary cessation doctrine.
subtopics: The unique nature of statutory penalties payable to the Commissioner rather than the plaintiff
Standing requirements: demonstrating injury for each claim and form of relief sought
The relationship between standing at commencement and mootness throughout litigation
The Friends of the Earth framework: civil penalties as redress for ongoing unlawful conduct
Deterrence value of penalties when violations are ongoing
The voluntary cessation doctrine and the 'absolutely clear' standard for mootness
The factual dispute about whether Consilio's violative overtime policy remains in effect
The court's decision to vacate and remand for the district court to determine jurisdiction

outline.chapter_title: The MWTA Claim, Injunctive Relief, and Preservation Issues
outline.description: This chapter addresses the court's treatment of Cohen's MWTA notice claim and request for injunctive relief, highlighting procedural requirements for preserving issues on appeal and properly amending claims.
subtopics: The MWTA claim: failure to provide statutorily required notice of a policy change
Cohen's failure to cite statutory authority for civil penalties under the MWTA
Waiver through inadequate appellate briefing: the Milligan standard
Cohen's shifting injunctive relief requests from complaint to summary judgment briefing
The district court's proper refusal to consider arguments raised for the first time in opposition briefs
Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 15(a) and proper procedures for amending claims
The court's affirmance of dismissal of the MWTA and injunctive relief claims
